themes.label: Profanity / taboo insults used for political or ideological contempt
defining_features: profanity_or_taboo_language (explicit vulgar insults, F-word, sexual/physiological vulgarity)
informal_register_or_slang (where present alongside profanity)
ridicule_or_mockery (often co-occurs with taboo language)
themes.interpretation: Posts that rely heavily on explicit profanity or taboo slurs/insults as the main rhetorical device form a strong moderation-relevant cluster, and appear more often in remove-rated examples than keep-rated ones.

themes.label: Outgroup vs ingroup “us vs them” or militant boogeyman framing
defining_features: us_vs_them_framing (in-group/out-group contrast such as “the rest of us” vs elites; or MAGA vs others)
target_directionality (explicit labeling of opposing groups)
victimhood_or_persecution_framing may appear when used to justify escalation
themes.interpretation: Group polarization language—especially when paired with dehumanizing or militant “boogeyman” constructs—shows up in both labels but more frequently in remove-rated content.

themes.label: Mockery/dehumanizing comparisons and competence insults
defining_features: ridicule_or_mockery (mocking illustrative scenarios, demeaning competence, animal/derisive personification)
dehumanizing comparison via scenario or labels
themes.interpretation: When posts attack opponents through ridicule, demeaning imagery, or competence contempt (rather than policy argument), they appear frequently in remove-rated examples.

themes.label: Targeted accusations involving sexual violence / child abuse allegations
defining_features: sexual_child_molestation_accusation (touching children’s genitals / grooming framing)
profanity_or_taboo_language co-occurring with sexual allegations
explicit taboo labels tied to sexual violence (e.g., “rapist”)
themes.interpretation: Explicit sexual-crime allegations—especially involving children—constitute a distinct high-risk theme and lean toward removal.

themes.label: Explicit calls to action (political pressure, voting instructions, or direct directives)
defining_features: call_to_action (vote/unelect; contact/pressure Congress; direct audience instructions)
pragmatics_intent (imperatives, “Will you join me…”, “Lock in your vote…”)
themes.interpretation: Action-oriented political mobilization appears in both groups; however, explicit voting/pressure instructions co-occur with other abusive/proscriptive elements more often in remove-rated content.

themes.label: Policy prescription and reform recommendations (often non-violent reform framing)
defining_features: policy_prescription_present (gun safety courses, electing majorities, enforcing laws, removing/relaxing restrictions, renewable energy plans)
primary_policy_domain (gun reform, climate, immigration, healthcare, education, etc.)
causal_claim_present sometimes used to justify policy
themes.interpretation: Moderation signals look calmer when content is primarily about reform/requirements (e.g., safety courses, energy transitions) rather than direct abuse; this cluster is predominantly keep-rated.

themes.label: Gun rights / gun reform / Second Amendment argumentation (including causal claims and detailed weapon mention)
defining_features: primary_policy_domain (gun policy / Second Amendment / gun reform)
causal_claim_present (policy changes linked to deaths)
list_or_enumeration (e.g., enumerating weapon components)
policy_prescription_present (remove/relax restrictions; safety course requirements)
themes.interpretation: Firearms/Second Amendment discourse forms a major topical theme; the moderation outcome varies depending on whether the rhetoric stays argumentative/prescriptive versus shifts into profanity/violent directives.

themes.label: Immigration enforcement, ICE/border issues, and refugee/DACA support
defining_features: primary_policy_domain (immigration / DACA / Dream Act / border enforcement)
hashtag_or_mention_pattern may appear (handles/addresses) but not required
target_directionality (ICE or enforcement groups targeted or defended)
call_to_action (urging support; contacting/pressure Congress)
themes.interpretation: Immigration enforcement discussions often co-occur with hostile language toward enforcement actors or direct support demands; this tends toward removal more often than keep in this shard.

themes.label: Conspiratorial or deception framing (media/power narratives, “manufactured outrage,” rigged systems)
defining_features: conspiratorial_framing (manufactured outrage; hidden information; rigged proceedings; deceptive power grabs)
factual_assertion_vs_speculation (may use categorical or speculative conspiracy claims)
ridicule_or_mockery can coexist
themes.interpretation: When posts frame institutions/legislation/media as deliberately deceptive or rigged, they skew strongly toward removal.

themes.label: Strong emotion, urgency, and emphatic formatting (all-caps, heavy punctuation, doom framing)
defining_features: all_caps_emphasis and/or high_punctuation_intensity
emphatic_outrage (doom/consequence warnings or imperative admonitions)
approximate_token_length_band can be long when used for extended justification
themes.interpretation: Urgent/emphatic style alone doesn’t determine moderation, but in combination with other contentious elements it is more common among remove-rated posts.

cross_cutting_themes: Profanity/sexual taboo intersects with target insults and dehumanizing ridicule (spanning multiple themes: 1, 3, 4, 2).
Us-vs-them framing frequently pairs with conspiracy or deception narratives about opposing actors (spanning themes: 2 and 9).

Policy prescription appears across topical domains (gun, climate, healthcare, immigration), but moderation outcome depends on whether rhetoric stays reformist/argumentative versus escalates to abuse/violence directives (themes: 6 with 1/2/10).

Second-person addressing, conditional/question structures (e.g., “Do you…?”, if/then hypotheticals) can be used both in keep-rated policy argumentation and in remove-rated accusatory/abusive rhetoric (spanning themes: 5/6 with 2/10).
Gun-related content (theme 7) often co-occurs with victimhood and urgency/doom framing when children/violence stakes are invoked (themes: 7 and 6/10/8).
